title: Reflexive routines
subtitle: Routines with other people
objectives: Use reflexive pronouns with routines and infinitives.
Distinguish an action on oneself from an action on another person.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c2-u01. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Who receives the action?
lectures.body: Me lavo describes washing myself; lavo los platos describes washing dishes. With a body part, Spanish commonly uses the definite article: Me lavo las manos, not a required possessive equivalent of my. Reflexive pronouns match the subject: me, te, se, nos, os, se. Place one before a conjugated verb or attach it to an infinitive: Me voy a levantar / Voy a levantarme. Both positions work in this construction; do not use both at once. A stem-changing reflexive verb keeps its verb pattern: me acuesto, nos acostamos. Not every se is reflexive; later courses distinguish other uses.

lectures.title: Routines are negotiable
lectures.body: Use primero, después, antes de and después de to organize a routine. After a preposition, a verb normally stays infinitive: antes de salir, después de ducharse. If a different subject follows, a finite clause is often needed; do not force every English before-sentence into an infinitive. In this unit keep the subject constant. To negotiate, state a need, ask about the other person’s need, and propose a sequence: Necesito ducharme antes de salir. ¿Te parece bien? This is more useful than listing activities without acknowledging a shared bathroom, transport schedule or caregiving responsibility.

lectures.title: Who performs the action, and who experiences it?
lectures.body:
In **Ana lava el coche**, the subject Ana washes something else. In **Ana se lava**, the subject also receives the action. In **Ana se lava las manos**, the body part appears with an article; the pronoun already identifies whose hands are involved. *Ana lava sus manos* is not a good mechanical replacement for the ordinary routine expression. Context can justify a possessive, but it is not the default pattern to memorize.

A two-verb phrase gives you two useful positions: **Me voy a acostar temprano** and **Voy a acostarme temprano**. The pronoun still refers to yo in both. You cannot attach **se** just because the dictionary prints **acostarse**: that **se** marks the dictionary form, not every speaker. Notice also **nos acostamos** versus **me acuesto**; choosing the pronoun does not eliminate the stem change.

Build a three-step account with **antes de**, **después de** and **luego**. After a preposition, use an infinitive: **Después de levantarme, desayuno**. Ask a partner one practical follow-up about time or sequence. This checks whether the routine is comprehensible beyond a memorized list.

reading:
—Me levanto a las seis y media. ¿Y tú?
—Normalmente a las siete, pero mañana necesito salir temprano.
—Entonces puedes ducharte primero. Yo preparo el desayuno.
—Gracias. Después de ducharme, voy a vestirme y preparar la mochila.
—¿Te acuestas temprano esta noche?
—Sí. Me acuesto a las diez. ¿Te parece bien usar el baño hasta las siete?
—Sí, pero necesito lavarme las manos antes de cocinar.
Resume el acuerdo: quién usa el baño, qué hace la otra persona y qué pequeña excepción necesitan prever.

worked.reason: The reflexive construction normally uses the definite article with the body part.
Nosotros retains o; the reflexive pronoun does not create a stem change.
Attach the matching me pronoun to the infinitive.
A preposition takes an infinitive here; the same person performs both actions.
The third-person subject requires the reflexive pronoun se.
Washing dishes is not an action performed on oneself; no reflexive pronoun is needed.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I wash my hands.
quiz.explanation: “Me lavo las manos” expresses “I wash my hands”. “Puedes ducharte primero” instead means “You can shower first”. “Lavo los platos” instead means “I wash the dishes”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: We go to bed early.
quiz.explanation: “Nos acostamos temprano” expresses “We go to bed early”. “Nos vemos a las siete” instead means “We will see each other at seven”. “Preparo el desayuno” instead means “I prepare breakfast”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I am going to shower.
quiz.explanation: “Voy a ducharme” expresses “I am going to shower”. “Me acuesto a las diez” instead means “I go to bed at ten”. “Tenemos que organizarnos” instead means “We have to organize ourselves”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I am going to shower (pronoun before verb).
quiz.explanation: “Me voy a duchar” expresses “I am going to shower (pronoun before verb)”. “Se levanta temprano” instead means “She or he gets up early”. “Me lavo las manos” instead means “I wash my hands”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: Before leaving.
quiz.explanation: “Antes de salir” expresses “Before leaving”. “Nos acostamos temprano” instead means “We go to bed early”. “Lavo los platos” instead means “I wash the dishes”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
answers: ["Antes de salir","¿Te parece bien?","Puedes ducharte primero"]
quiz.explanation: “Antes de salir” means “Before leaving”. “¿Te parece bien?” means “Does that work for you?”. “Puedes ducharte primero” means “You can shower first”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Plan a shared morning with a partner. Each person has one non-negotiable need; find a workable order and confirm it. Solo: create two schedules and explain how you resolved a conflict.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Me lavo las manos / Nos acostamos temprano. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Plan a shared morning with a partner. Each person has one non-negotiable need; find a workable order and confirm it. Solo: create two schedules and explain how you resolved a conflict.
culture: Daily routines depend on work, climate, family and personal circumstances. Avoid treating a textbook’s timetable as a national norm. Ask individuals about their needs rather than predicting them from nationality.
selfAssessment: I can use reflexive pronouns with routines and infinitives.
I can distinguish an action on oneself from an action on another person.
I can negotiate a practical shared routine.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
